PRODUCT & ARCHITECTURE

MIDNIGHT EXPRESS / PRIVATE WORKFLOW COORDINATION

Private workflow
coordination.

Midnight Express is a proposed network and software toolkit for exchanging confidential business updates between applications, organizations and software agents.

When a quote, payment or approval passes between organizations, each application needs to know who sent it, whether it is current and what action it permits. Express would carry signed, encrypted updates and help applications recover their progress after an interruption. Receivers would identify relevant updates locally, keeping business subscription filters away from delivery operators.

First proposed pilot: quote coordination Local prototypes · production integration pending
See a business workflow Explore the architecture

01 / WHAT IT IS

A delivery layer for
confidential business updates.

Starting with teams connecting backend and desktop quote systems, finance software and human-approved agents.

Business updates become signed events.

A dealer sends an offer that a buyer can compare. A bank sends payment status that a finance system can match to an invoice. Express would carry these events between authorized participants, with the information needed to check their source and meaning.

Your application decides what happens next.

Authorized recipients recognize relevant messages using their own keys. Their applications check the sender, permissions, expiry and current workflow state before taking an action. Delivery is an input to that decision.

Where Midnight fits

Publication admission determines whether a member may send a message through the network within its quota. The proposed Midnight Registry records the memberships used to check that proof. The receiving application separately checks whether the sender may request a business action. If that action changes a contract, the contract also needs proof of authority and protection against repeated execution. Batch anchors supply ledger evidence for that path; ordinary coordination can finish off-chain without a ledger transaction for every update.

Privacy scope: authorized endpoints can read their shared content. Connections, shard participation, timing and envelope sizes may remain visible. Local recognition requires receivers to handle additional traffic; bandwidth, integration and operating costs are part of the pilot evaluation.

02 / THE PROBLEM

Keep track of work
across applications.

Teams need an agreed record of current terms, completed work and valid approvals when their applications exchange updates.

01 / CONFIDENTIALITY

Share the update with the right participants.

Quotes, invoice amounts and approval instructions can reveal sensitive relationships. Topic names and subscription filters can also reveal what a participant is watching.

Design response: encrypt business details and let receivers recognize relevant events locally.

02 / CONTINUITY

Recover the last valid workflow state.

Disconnects, retries and updates from several systems can leave teams comparing records or chasing status. The latest received message may not be the latest valid state.

Design response: retained history, explicit gaps and durable endpoint progress, with duplicate and expiry checks.

03 / PERMISSION

Know what an approval permits.

A delivered or authentic message may still request an unauthorized action. An approval needs a specific signer, target, budget and deadline.

Design response: signed business intent and application policy, plus consumer proofs for contract effects.

The value to test is fewer manual handoffs and less reconciliation effort while preserving confidentiality and correct decisions. Customer demand, savings and operating economics remain unvalidated.

03 / SEE THE WORK

How the proposed pilots
would work.

Illustrative pilot scenarios. Quotes come first; invoice matching and agent approvals test reuse of the foundation.

A buyer asks two approved dealers for prices.

A request for quote (RFQ) asks what price a dealer will offer for a particular transaction.

  1. Request

    The buyer sends a confidential request with a response deadline to approved dealers.

  2. Compare

    Dealers return signed offers with expiry times. The buyer’s application checks roles and current terms.

  3. Accept and hand off

    The buyer explicitly accepts one valid offer. The agreed terms go to the separately authorized settlement process.

First scope: backend and desktop quote coordination and off-chain acceptance. Automated settlement requires separate authority and replay checks.

Across these scenarios, recovery is intended to resume retained updates and stored workflow progress after an interruption. It needs verified endpoint processing; older history and gaps require explicit handling.

04 / WHERE IT COULD HELP

Three proposed pilots
and seven further candidates.

These candidates are recommendations. Customer results and launch commitments have not been established. Ranking considers confidentiality, shared stack reuse, measurable outcomes and additional dependencies.

Expand a card for the people involved, the trigger, first scope, evaluation measures and remaining work.

01
Proposed pilot a

Request and compare confidential quotes

A buyer requests prices from approved dealers, compares signed offers and records an explicit acceptance.

Who is involved

Buyer, approved dealers, compliance reviewer and settlement operations.

What starts it

buyer requests a priced offer; dealers reply; buyer accepts one signed offer.

Illustrative scenario

Two dealers respond to the same request. The buyer accepts one valid offer before it expires and hands the agreed terms to the existing settlement process. The proposed recovery layer should preserve that accepted record after an interruption.

Value to test

Less disclosure of trade intent and counterparties; shorter reconciliation and settlement handoff.

First useful scope

Start with requests, signed quotes, expiry and off-chain acceptance; enable settlement only after authority/replay/anchored-binding gates.

How we would measure it

Quote turnaround, reconciliation effort and successful outage recovery.

Scope boundary

The first scope coordinates quotes and off-chain acceptance. A receipt does not mean the trade settled.

What must be proven

First design partner; CON-060 and contract adapter gate automated settlement.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + private schemas + signed roles + local recovery

Requirement identity: UC-01 · Institutional RFQ and negotiated quote coordination

02
Proposed pilot b

Match invoices to payment status

Finance teams connect signed invoice updates to authenticated payment notices and investigate mismatches.

Who is involved

Supplier finance team, customer treasury and a bank or payment-service integration.

What starts it

invoice issued, approved, paid, disputed or refunded.

Illustrative scenario

A supplier receives a payment notice for a particular invoice. The application checks the reference and amount before marking it paid. A wrong amount remains unresolved, and repeated notices must not create extra accounting entries.

Value to test

Reduce manual matching while protecting amounts, account relationships and invoice contents.

First useful scope

Match invoices and authenticated payment-status notices; no automatic payment execution in initial pilot.

How we would measure it

Unmatched invoices, manual handling time and duplicate postings.

Scope boundary

The initial scope matches status and records. Authenticated payment evidence, finance integration and destination duplicate protection are required.

What must be proven

ERP integration and authenticated payment evidence; destination idempotency for external effects.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + durable processing + ERP/payment adapter

Requirement identity: UC-03 · Invoice, payment-status and reconciliation workflows

03
Proposed pilot c

Coordinate agents with human approval

An agent proposes a bounded action; a person approves a specific target, budget and expiry.

Who is involved

Enterprise worker, AI or business agent, approval officer and sandbox executor.

What starts it

agent proposes purchase, settlement, access grant or other bounded action.

Illustrative scenario

A procurement agent requests a purchase from one supplier within a budget. A person signs that exact scope. The executor rejects a different supplier, an excessive amount or an expired approval, even when the message is authentic.

Value to test

Automate multi-party work with accountable approvals and protected instructions.

First useful scope

Agent proposes a bounded action; human signs an expiring approval; sandbox executor enforces target and budget.

How we would measure it

Approval cycle time, manual handoffs and rejected unauthorized/replayed actions.

Scope boundary

The application must verify agent output and enforce permission before acting on a delivered message.

What must be proven

Application capability enforcement and trusted human approval UI; contract effects require consumer proof.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + signed action policy + durable processing

Requirement identity: UC-05 · Agent coordination with bounded human approvals

Further candidates

04
Candidate · next

Keep credential and access status current

An issuer or employer sends authenticated changes so verifiers can update their access decisions.

Who is involved

Credential issuer, subject wallet and service or employer verifier.

What starts it

credential issued/expired/revoked or staff/partner removed.

Illustrative scenario

A contractor’s credential is revoked. Services receive a newer authenticated issuer version that overrides a delayed earlier grant. A service with outdated evidence would report stale status and block high-risk access.

Value to test

Reduce stale authorization while avoiding public subscription graph.

First useful scope

Propagate authenticated issuer epochs to backend verifiers and mark stale state explicitly.

How we would measure it

Stale authorization interval, update coverage and membership-change recovery.

Scope boundary

Receiving a notice is not completed revocation. Tested enforcement and rekeying govern future access; past copies remain possible.

What must be proven

Issuer authority, stale-cache policy and tested removal/rekey; event receipt is not revocation completion.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + issuer adapter + group/rekey policy

Requirement identity: UC-06 · Credential and access-revocation coordination

05
Candidate · next

Resolve procurement and delivery exceptions

A buyer, supplier and logistics team share restricted milestones and agree the next step after a delay.

Who is involved

Purchasing manager, supplier, logistics provider and authorized insurer or auditor.

What starts it

purchase order accepted, delivery milestone reached, delay/temperature anomaly detected.

Illustrative scenario

A supplier reports that required parts will arrive late. The logistics team shares a revised estimate with the people handling the order. The buyer records an acknowledged next step without spreading unrelated commercial terms.

Value to test

Faster exception resolution with limited sharing of commercial counterparties and terms.

First useful scope

Share signed delivery milestones and restricted exception notices among buyer, supplier and logistics actors.

How we would measure it

Exception resolution time, missed handoffs and connector integration effort.

Scope boundary

A signature identifies the report’s source. Physical shipment evidence, partner integrations and history policies need separate validation.

What must be proven

Authenticated gateways and archive/key policy; sensor provenance does not prove physical truth.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + group roles + connector schemas + history policy

Requirement identity: UC-07 · Procurement and supply-chain exception coordination

06
Candidate · ledger-gated

Follow contract milestones privately

A desktop application distinguishes a received notice from a verified contract milestone.

Who is involved

Application user, desktop wallet or application and contract observer.

What starts it

contract event such as settlement completion, escrow milestone or authorization change.

Illustrative scenario

A user is waiting for an escrow milestone. The application shows an update as pending, then confirms it only after checking the exact ledger event and successful application. Retained notices would let the application catch up after a disconnect.

Value to test

Timely useful notifications without publishing subscription interests or exposing private business data.

First useful scope

Desktop/backend public-event or signed-application pilot first; private carried events follow underlying Midnight capability.

How we would measure it

Finality-label correctness, missed-event recovery and application integration time.

Scope boundary

Start with public-event or signed-application notices. Private carried events and private mobile reception require further platform work.

What must be proven

Private carried-event capability, exact-byte/applied-phase verification; private mobile delivery is separately gated.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + finalized Midnight adapter + listener SDK

Requirement identity: UC-02 · Private contract lifecycle notifications

07
Candidate · connector-gated

Coordinate sensitive incident response

Authorized responders exchange incident updates and record who owns the next investigation step.

Who is involved

Operations lead, service owner, chain or service integration and response team.

What starts it

service degradation, key compromise, delayed settlement or chain interruption.

Illustrative scenario

A settlement service stops progressing. Responders exchange private status updates and assign a human-reviewed investigation step. A returning responder would recover retained notices to catch up on the handoff.

Value to test

Faster coordinated response with protected incident details and less dependence on one public notification provider.

First useful scope

Coordinate human-reviewed response using an independent emergency channel alongside MPE.

How we would measure it

Response handoff time, recovered notices and failed-handler isolation.

Scope boundary

Keep an independent emergency channel. Delivery, source trust, funding and failure isolation must be validated.

What must be proven

Declared cross-chain trust/finality, funded operators and alternate emergency path.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + failure isolation + encrypted quarantine + connector trust

Requirement identity: UC-10 · Confidential incident and cross-chain operations coordination

08
Candidate · policy-gated

Review proposals and collect approvals

A board or committee coordinates confidential review and records explicit approvals under its own rules.

Who is involved

Board or DAO committee, authorized reviewers and execution agent.

What starts it

proposal submitted, confidential review requested, approval threshold met.

Illustrative scenario

A committee reviews a vendor proposal under an illustrative three-approval policy. Two approvals, an expired approval or a delivery receipt cannot satisfy that policy. The application checks valid authority before execution and prepares narrowly scoped audit evidence.

Value to test

Coordinate sensitive deliberation and auditable authorization without exposing reviewer watchlists.

First useful scope

Coordinate confidential review and collect explicit approvals; execution policy remains application-owned.

How we would measure it

Review completion time, complete approval evidence and replay rejection.

Scope boundary

The customer defines and enforces the approval threshold. Anonymous voting and ledger execution require separate evidence; ledger execution also needs consumer proof.

What must be proven

Threshold/multisig authority, selective disclosure and CON-060 before on-chain execution; no anonymous voting claim.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + group roles + signed threshold policy

Requirement identity: UC-09 · Private governance review and approval workflows

09
Candidate · freshness/mobile-gated

Review portfolio and collateral warnings

An account owner receives advisory risk updates with visible source age and gap status.

Who is involved

Account owner, risk service and an explicitly authorized delegated agent.

What starts it

margin breach, liquidation risk, expiring order or abnormal exposure.

Illustrative scenario

A desktop risk application reports collateral below the owner’s threshold. The owner checks the underlying account before deciding whether to add collateral. A stale or incomplete feed is shown as such and blocks high-risk automated effects.

Value to test

Earlier intervention without broadcasting portfolio/watchlist to notification infrastructure.

First useful scope

Backend advisory alerts first; block automated effects on stale/gapped feeds.

How we would measure it

Alert freshness, gap detection and recipient intervention time.

Scope boundary

Advisory backend/desktop alerts first. Freshness and market integrations must be measured; there is no liquidation-prevention guarantee.

What must be proven

Reliable market connectors and proven budgets; no hard-real-time liquidation guarantee; private phones need retrieval.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + source snapshot/delta adapters + freshness guards

Requirement identity: UC-04 · Portfolio and collateral risk alerts

10
Candidate · sector-gated

Keep insurance claim handoffs moving

Claims handlers and adjusters exchange status updates and authorized references to encrypted documents.

Who is involved

Claimant, insurer, adjuster and authorized payment or reinsurance partner.

What starts it

claim submitted, evidence requested, assessment completed or payment approved.

Illustrative scenario

An adjuster requests a repair estimate. The claims handler shares an authorized document reference with the assigned adjuster. An assessment update moves the claim to its next review step while role permissions limit the evidence shared.

Value to test

Faster multi-party processing with narrowed exposure of claimant facts.

First useful scope

Exchange status and authorized encrypted-document references among claimant, insurer and adjuster.

How we would measure it

Claim handoff time, missing-document requests and duplicate payment prevention.

Scope boundary

Claims decisions, payment permission and retention policy remain with the insurer. Access withdrawal or event expiry does not erase copies already obtained.

What must be proven

Customer data/retention policy, encrypted object integration and authorized retrieval; expiry does not erase copies.

Integration dependencies

MPE coordination + role-scoped attachments + long-history policy

Requirement identity: UC-08 · Insurance claim handoffs and milestones

05 / HOW THE STACK SUPPORTS THE WORK

What each component
is responsible for.

The overlay distributes sealed events. Endpoints recognize relevant updates and apply their own rules. Select a component to see its role and remaining integration work.

APPLICATION ENDPOINT Private business context
Sealed event + one admission proof
DISTRIBUTION OVERLAY Opaque envelopes

GossipSub fans out in parallel to retained stores, whole-shard receivers and the Midnight anchor.

Whole-shard reception → recognize locally
RECEIVING ENDPOINT Authorized processing
Optional effect: workflow authority + anchor evidence
PARALLEL LEDGER BRANCH Independent inclusion evidence

Members receive a publication allowance for each envelope size class. One rate-limiting nullifier (RLN) proof binds a publication to a permitted class credit and proves registered membership without identifying the publisher. Group security protects session content inside the encrypted payload. This map shows proposed integrations.

01

Privacy at the endpoints

Event semantics stay encrypted. Receivers recognize relevant events using local keys, so relays do not need their business subscription filters.

02

Recovery before action

The receiving application would store its progress and replay retained updates after an interruption. An external system must also prevent a retry from creating a second effect.

03

Authority is explicit

Encryption and anchor inclusion do not grant permission. Authorized signed instructions and application policy define permission. A consumer contract checks that permission, message binding and replay protection.

06 / THE PROTOCOL JOURNEY

What happens beneath
the business workflow.

A technical walkthrough of publication, local reception and recovery. Retention and anchoring proceed independently; contract effects add a separate proof path.

Each stage supplies different evidence

Admission · persistence · anchor/finality · local processing · signed business acknowledgement

These are independent facts. An inclusion proof does not establish delivery, availability or business completion.

07 / RECOVERY FOUNDATION

Resume the workflow
after an interruption.

A receiving application needs a durable record of what it processed and what remains to do. UmbraDB, which understands Midnight data, and PostgreSQL are the proposed foundation for trusted Node backend hosts. UmbraDB supplies temporal records, checkpoints and cursors for that work.

A local Umbra/PostgreSQL prototype now commits one report-row effect, deduplication, outbox, checkpoint and cursor through the public transaction API. Full MPE recovery still needs authenticated processing, protected restore and writer ownership enforced at commit, alongside the proposed future-release requirements.

Tested locally: report row + progress Remaining: full MPE recovery

SQLite serves standalone Rust nodes and clients. The custom MPE store protocol separately handles replicated opaque envelopes and persistence receipts.

08 / FROM PROPOSAL TO PRODUCT

From a workflow demo
to production evidence.

FIRST DEMONSTRATION

Quote coordination

Requests, signed quotes, expiry and off-chain acceptance on backend and desktop. Internal demonstrations may use clearly labeled mock membership and admission. Measure turnaround, manual handoffs and outage recovery.

REUSE PILOTS

Invoices and agent approvals

Match invoices to authenticated payment status; enforce expiring human approvals in a sandbox. Set targets against actual customer baselines and test duplicate, stale and unauthorized messages.

BEFORE PRODUCTION

Prove the coordination core

Real finalized membership, accepted admission proofs, measured limits, replicated retention, signed receipts and funded operators. Verify durable endpoint processing through the proposed Umbra capability or an equivalent composition.

Requirements for the later extensions

OpenMLS group security needs identity, epoch and recovery tests. Contract effects need signed authority, replay protection and binding to an anchored message. Private contract-origin events and mobile reception depend on additional platform and retrieval work. These tracks can proceed alongside coordination, with their own acceptance gates.

Why these dependencies

Semaphore supplies membership lifecycle patterns; publication uses one combined proof. Signal remains a deferred pairwise alternative; OpenMLS is the selected group extension. Kafka, NATS and RabbitMQ inform delivery semantics; the stack does not require those services.

QUESTIONS / IN PLAIN LANGUAGE

What a design partner
should know.

Who is the first audience?

Teams building institutional backend and desktop workflows: quote coordination, invoice reconciliation and human-approved agents. Wallet, contract and mobile experiences are part of the broader portfolio, with separate readiness requirements.

What would Express add to an existing event system?

The proposed combination is encrypted business events, local recognition that keeps subscription interests away from delivery infrastructure, anonymous accountable publication admission, and recoverable endpoint processing. Existing brokers can encrypt payloads; private matching, metadata exposure and workflow permissions need their own evaluation.

What does “private” cover?

Business contents and subscription interests under the selected profile. Connection, shard, timing and size information can remain observable. The symmetric launch profile does not establish forward secrecy or origin anonymity; private mobile reception remains research-dependent.

How do delivery and business completion differ?

A message can be relayed or stored before anyone acts on it. The receiving application checks business policy and records progress. An accepted offer, verified payment match or authorized execution is a distinct result, with an explicit signed acknowledgement when the workflow requires one.

What is available now?

The project has a v0.2 conformance reference and bounded local prototypes: strict data contracts, independent RFQ interpretation, read-only chain projections and tested Umbra/PostgreSQL report-row recovery. Explore the Data Model guide for shared meaning and scope. Complete Express integration, production authentication/admission, live finality and authorized contract effects still require acceptance evidence.

How would we judge a pilot?

Agree a real customer baseline, then measure turnaround and staff effort alongside correctness, outage recovery, duplicate handling, integration cost and operating cost. A useful result improves the agreed workflow without sacrificing valid permissions or losing progress. No savings percentage or performance target is established yet.

A few useful terms
Event
An update that another application can respond to.
Endpoint
The participating application or host where keys, private business context and processing policy live.
Local recognition
Identifying relevant messages using keys at the receiver, without giving the relay a business subscription filter.
Request for quote (RFQ)
Asking approved dealers what price they will offer for a specified transaction.
Reconciliation
Checking that invoice, payment and accounting records agree.
Duplicate protection / idempotency
Ensuring a repeated update does not create another effect, using the receiving application or destination’s rules.
Anchor
A batch commitment recorded on Midnight that can support inclusion evidence.
Finality
The point at which ledger evidence is accepted as settled under the chosen chain policy.

DESIGN & EVIDENCE

Design documents
and implementation evidence.

The stack is a recommendation with tested local components. Production deployment and protocol performance remain to be demonstrated; the selected libraries need integration.
